title: One control, one action: Revoke / Cancel invitation / Decline request are stored and recorded as themselves, and a role change leaves a record (the question-generation Retry half was removed with the generator, 10/10/2026)
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/seat-actions.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/seats-pages.test.mjs packages/core/tracy-core/test/roster.test.mjs packages/core/tracy-core/test/team-actions.test.mjs
S2: Read the exit code of each command and the '# fail' and '# skipped' lines of its TAP output.
expect: The command exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# skipped 0'.

seat-actions: 'DELETE {kind: cancel_invite} stores cancel_invite, answers it, and closes the seat' and its revoke and decline_request siblings pass: the row carries removal_kind = the kind sent, revoked_at is set, declined_at stays null, the answer is {revoked: true, kind}.

seat-actions: 'an explicit kind that does not match the row is refused and nothing is written' passes: 409 {code: 'SEAT_STATE_CHANGED', kind: <the kind the row calls for>}, no UPDATE, no ops_signal row.

seat-actions: 'a successful revoke records team.revoke with the actor, the site and the target' and its two siblings pass, and 'a role change records team.role_change with the role it left and the role it took' passes; 'an unchanged role, an invalid role and a refused change record nothing' passes.

seat-actions: 'DELETE with no body (an older tab) runs the act the row calls for, revoke, and stores it as that' and its siblings (no body and content-length: 0; each for revoke, cancel_invite and decline_request) pass: 200 {revoked: true, kind: <the kind the row calls for>}, removal_kind is that kind, one ops_signal row team.<kind>. 'DELETE with empty object is refused where the row calls for revoke: nothing removed, recorded or synced' and its siblings (a whitespace body, a single space, a newline, a declared length with nothing in it, a chunked body with nothing in it, a kind beside another key, a kind under another name; each for the three kinds) pass: a body that was sent, even one holding nothing, is not the bodyless call: 400 {code: 'INVALID_REQUEST'}, no UPDATE, no ops_signal row, no seat_sync row.

seat-actions: 'a tab that names its act is told when the row has moved on; a bodyless one keeps its v1 meaning' passes: an invitation accepted while the dialog was open answers 409 {code: 'SEAT_STATE_CHANGED', kind: 'revoke'} to {kind: 'cancel_invite'} and keeps revoked_at null; a body without a known kind answers 400; the bodyless call of an older tab answers 200 and is stored and recorded as revoke (known, accepted limit of v1 compatibility).
team-actions: 'action.cancelInvite: the confirm step names that act and the write sends {kind: cancel_invite}' and its two siblings pass: one DELETE whose JSON body is exactly {kind}.

selectors.remove_door: DELETE /api/sites/:key/seats/:grant with body {kind} (no body at all: the v1 call, kind read from the row)

evidence: Issue #792 (QA audit, re-verified on develop f9c734938): three labels over one bodyless DELETE that wrote revoked_at for all of them; no opsFor.record in the DELETE and PATCH handlers; Retry called press(view.job.mode) with the set and feedback on screen. Replayed on base cb76d6c6d with these same test files: the cases named above fail there. Review follow-up: a body that was sent with a key beside kind was still accepted, and the fields of a press were judged after being cut or defaulted; replayed on the tree as it was before that fix, those cases fail there by assertion. Compatibility (v1 is not broken): a DELETE with no body and a press naming only a mode are still answered with the meaning they had on the base, and are stored as the act that ran; a client loaded before this change can therefore still send an inferred removal, which is closed for every client built from this change on.
fence: The real seatsRoutes handlers with the real ops-signal service over an in-memory pool double, and the real TeamView mounted on a DOM double with a fetch fixture. Not covered here: PostgreSQL (migration 053, its check constraints, the last-owner trigger, a real race), a real host's seat door, a real browser.
